name: Arienzo
what: The home parish. The Collegiate Church of Sant'Andrea Apostolo holds baptisms from 1672, marriages from 1754 and deaths from 1733. Every Falco generation from Pasquale to Raffaele was born, married and buried here.

name: San Felice a Cancello
what: Birthplace of Angela Rosa Morgillo, who married into the line in the 1840s. The next comune west of Arienzo.

name: Arpaia
what: Across the provincial border, four kilometres from Arienzo. Carmine Falco and Francesca Zampiello were married here on 15 January 1955 — the Comune's own extract of marriage act n. 1, which corrected this archive's earlier «Benevento». Gerardo Falco was born here in 1913; the Zampiello family were here through the 1920s and 1930s.

name: Forchia
what: Filomena Annecchino was born here on 10 April 1897 — dated by her own Italian passport of 1972 («nato a Forchia il 10-4-1897»), and before that only from her Brisbane grave. Her birth act has never been found: Antenati holds no Forchia births for 1897 in any fondo. Her son Raffaele, born 25 August 1925, is still dated only from his Brisbane grave and Queensland death registration. The family is documented here to 1937, when Carminantonio declared his infant son Aniello's death at Contrada Case Sparse 68 (act 17, 2 August 1937).

name: Benevento
what: The provincial capital — and NOT, as this archive said until October 2026, the place where Carmine Falco and Francesca Zampiello married: that was Arpaia. Forchia and Arpaia lie in its province. Its Questura issued Filomena Annecchino's passport in July 1972 and Carminantonio Falco's on 5 August 1976, and stamped renewals in 1977 and 1978. Capital of the Lombard duchy that gave southern Italy the personal name Falco.

name: Brisbane
what: Where the line ends. Carmine arrived 26 March 1964, his mother Filomena on 5 February 1968, his father Carminantonio on 19 May 1969. Four of them are buried at Nudgee Cemetery — Carminantonio (d. 1985) and Filomena (d. 1988) in adjoining plots, their son Raffaele (d. 1988) and his wife Caterina Zampiello (d. 2004) in another pair.

name: Moiano
what: 1,296 register rows, from the Antenati name index — 310 Falco and 215 Annecchino. NO KINSHIP IS CLAIMED: the Moiano Falco and the Moiano Annecchino were harvested precisely to test whether either joined this family, and both are separate stocks. The town is listed because the archive holds records here, not because the line passes through it.

name: Paolisi
what: 511 register rows. Also the oldest unresolved question in the archive: Francesco Falco of Paolisi, 1714–1726, is the earliest Arienzo Falco household with a stated origin, and the dates would allow him to be Matteo's grandfather. No document joins them and this archive has not joined them.

name: Santa Maria a Vico
what: The parish of Santa Maria ad Nives, where Domenico Falco — son of the OTHER Giuseppe Falco, of strada Costa — married Mariantonia Frasca on 1 July 1844. Thirty-odd rows. It matters as a control: it is where the Falco this archive is not descended from can be found.

name: Cervinara
what: Thin — about a dozen rows, all from the Arienzo civil registers where a Cervinara birth or spouse is named in passing. No household here has been reconstructed.

name: Durazzano
what: Thin — about a dozen rows. Named in Arienzo acts as a place of origin; nothing more has been read here.

name: Airola
what: TWO ROWS, and they are listed to be honest about how little that is. The archive's only Airola material is an 1883 mention in the Benevento civil series.

name: Cervino
what: ONE ROW. Named once, in 1843. Listed so the atlas does not imply the archive has looked here and found nothing — it has barely looked.
